original_issue: The original finance concept is correct, but it is too thin for training usefulness because it lacks the operational reasoning behind the formula: how expected return, expected inflation, risk premium, and planning horizon change the practical interpretation of present value and discount rate choice.
proposed_fix: Expand time-value-of-money rationale to include investment return, rate/inflation sensitivity, and horizon dependency alongside the existing formula.
updated_content: Money today is worth more than the same nominal amount in the future because it can be invested to earn a return; retaining liquidity also avoids forced future consumption at unfavorable prices. Present value therefore depends not only on the formula PV = FV/(1+r)^n, but also on the expected real return after inflation, the chosen discount rate, and the planning horizon over which cash flows are compared.
revision_notes: Expansion preserves the original factual core (time value of money = investment return rationale). Adds three dimensions: (1) investment return rationale — why money today is worth more; (2) rate/inflation sensitivity — real vs nominal discount rate; (3) horizon dependency — planning horizon impact on present value.
